newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australian June company profits revised down.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australian June company profits revised down.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Statistics said on Thursday it had revised down June quarter company profits by A$671 million, the March quarter by A$124 and the December quarter by A$30 million.
If no other data were revised, the company profits revisions imply a change to negative growth in real GDP-A in the June quarter.
"The cause was late responses and also some respondents revising their figures," a bureau spokeswoman told Reuters.
Company profits data is published after a certain cut-off date for survey results.
The bureau then chases companies in the survey that have not responded in time and, in this case, found strongly negative data, the spokeswoman said.

The September quarter data, virtually unchanged from the revised-down June quarter, implies zero contribution to quarterly growth in nominal GDP-I, the income measure of economic activity, from large incorporated businesses.
The survey, limited to large incorporated businesses, does not match the comprehensive measure of profits in GDP data, gross operating surplus (GOS).
No data for other businesses will be available before September quarter GDP is published on December 4.

However, that residue grew by A$762 million in the June quarer. If one assumed it continued that trend behaviour, then the contribution of GOS to nominal quarterly growth in GDP-I would be 0.7 percentage points.
This is stronger than economists were typically expecting but from the now weaker base of the revised June quarter.
With the revisions, June quarter growth in company profits has weakened by A$547 million, implying a 0.5-percentage-point reduction in quarterly GDP-I growth.
But economic policy focuses on GDP-A, the average of GDP-I and the expenditure and production measures of GDP (GDP-E and GDP-P).
The effect of the revisions on GDP-A growth would therefore be only a third of the effect on GDP-I; that is, GDP-A would lose about 0.2 percentage points.
June quarter GDP-A growth, 0.1 percent, was barely positive, so the profits data imply a revision to negative GDP growth.
Annual GDP growth, the change between the September quarters of 1995 and 1996, will suffer a larger downward revision, because December and March quarter profits were also revised down.
The total downward revision for profits for the year to September 1996 was A$825 million, about 0.8 percent of quarterly GDP.
